title: The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Distracting Information in Long-Context Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2605.10828v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As large language models are increasingly deployed in retrieval-augmented generation and agentic systems that accumulate extensive context, understanding how distracting information affects long-context performance becomes critical. Prior work shows that semantically relevant yet misleading documents degrade performance, but the quantitative relationship between the proportion of distractors and performance remains unstudied. In this work, we systematically vary the hard-distractor proportion in fixed-length contexts, revealing a striking nonlinear pattern: as the proportion of hard distractors increases, performance drops sharply within the first small fraction, while the remainder of the range yields only marginal additional decline. translated_title: 第一滴墨水：长上下文推理中干扰信息的非线性影响
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型越来越多地部署在检索增强生成和累积大量上下文的智能体系统中，理解干扰信息如何影响长上下文性能变得至关重要。先前的研究表明，语义相关但具有误导性的文档会降低性能，但干扰物比例与性能之间的定量关系尚未被研究。在本工作中，我们系统地在固定长度上下文中变化硬干扰物比例，揭示了一个显著的非线性模式：随着硬干扰物比例增加，性能在第一个小比例范围内急剧下降，而剩余范围内仅产生边际额外的下降。我们将此称为“第一滴墨水”效应，类比于一滴墨水污染整杯水。我们的理论和实证分析基于注意力机制，表明硬干扰物会显著干扰模型的注意力分配，导致性能非线性退化。
tldr: 本文发现长上下文推理中，硬干扰物比例在最初小范围内即引发性能急剧下降，后续增加影响微弱，并命名为“第一滴墨水”效应，基于注意力机制解释了这一非线性现象。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a striking nonlinear pattern in long-context reasoning where performance drops sharply within the first small fraction of hard distractors and then plateaus, termed the "First Drop of Ink" effect, explained through attention mechanics.
